skill.name: spec-driven-implementation
skill.description: Drive a spec-first workflow for substantial features by writing PRODUCT.md before implementation, writing TECH.md when warranted, and keeping both specs updated as implementation evolves. Use when starting a significant feature, planning agent-driven implementation, or when the user wants product and tech specs checked into source control.
skill.summary: Plan substantial features with product and technical specifications, then keep those specifications aligned with implementation.
skill.author: warpdotdev

content.value_statement: Substantial feature work can become ambiguous when product intent, technical decisions, and implementation drift apart. This skill guides agents through practical product and technical specifications that stay aligned with shipped work.
actual_capabilities: Helps decide whether a feature needs a product or technical specification.
Structures PRODUCT.md around behavior, edge cases, success criteria, and validation.
Structures TECH.md around architecture, tradeoffs, risks, and testing.
Guides agents to implement from approved specifications.
Prompts teams to update specifications when implementation changes.
Connects specification review with tests and other verification artifacts.
limitations: It does not create or modify application code by itself.
It does not access Linear or other project tools without available integrations.
It cannot validate implementation behavior without repository tests or other evidence.
It does not replace product, architecture, or security review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Large Feature
use_cases.description: Turn an ambiguous feature request into a product spec, a technical plan when needed, and clear validation criteria.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Implementation
use_cases.description: Give coding agents stable behavioral and technical context before they implement a cross-cutting change.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering teams using AI coding tools

use_cases.title: Keep Documentation Current
use_cases.description: Review implementation changes and update the relevant specifications so the repository describes the behavior that actually ships.

prompt_templates.title: Decide If Specs Are Needed
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this feature request for size, ambiguity, and risk. Recommend whether to write PRODUCT.md, TECH.md, both, or neither. Explain the decision briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Product Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PRODUCT.md for this feature. Cover the user problem, intended behavior, invariants, edge cases, success criteria, and validation approach. Keep implementation details separate.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Technical Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the approved product behavior and repository context, draft a TECH.md for this feature. Document architecture, interfaces, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, rollout, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Specs Against Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare PRODUCT.md and TECH.md with the current implementation and tests. List behavior or architecture drift, then propose precise spec updates and missing verification.

output_examples.input: We need a new workspace invitation flow with several permission states and an uncertain rollout.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: write PRODUCT.md first and TECH.md after the permission model is settled. The request has user-facing edge cases, cross-cutting behavior, and rollout risk.

output_examples.input: The implementation now supports invitation expiration, but PRODUCT.md does not mention it.
output: Update PRODUCT.md with expiration behavior and recovery rules.
Add success criteria for expired invitations.
Add tests that cover expiration and re-invitation.

output_examples.input: The feature spans API, persistence, background jobs, and the client.
output_examples.output: TECH.md should document boundaries, data flow, failure handling, dependencies, rollout sequencing, and the test strategy before implementation begins.

best_practices: Write product behavior before choosing implementation details.
Use a technical specification when boundaries, tradeoffs, or risks are meaningful.
Update specifications whenever shipped behavior or architecture changes.
anti_patterns: Do not write specifications for routine changes that gain no clarity from them.
Do not let technical details replace user-facing behavior and success criteria.
Do not leave specifications unchanged after implementation diverges from the plan.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for substantial, ambiguous, cross-cutting, or risky feature work where shared written context improves implementation and review.

faq.question: Is a technical specification always required?
faq.answer: No. Use TECH.md when architecture, tradeoffs, dependencies, or testing decisions need explicit documentation.

faq.question: What belongs in PRODUCT.md?
faq.answer: Describe the user problem, desired behavior, invariants, edge cases, success criteria, and how the result will be validated.

faq.question: What belongs in TECH.md?
faq.answer: Describe implementation boundaries, interfaces, architecture, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, rollout, and testing.

faq.question: Can this skill implement the feature?
faq.answer: It guides implementation from approved specifications, but the implementation requires a coding agent and the target repository.

faq.question: How do I keep specifications accurate?
faq.answer: Compare them with code and tests during implementation, then update them whenever behavior, architecture, risks, or validation changes.
